title: MiniCPM5-2B on Jetson Orin Nano 8 GB - Full Benchmark Report
author: Hermes Agent for Walker Kirkpatrick

elements.text: MiniCPM5-2B on Jetson Orin Nano 8 GB

Full benchmark report: 64K baseline A-D suite, DSpark speculative decoding, and a maxed-out 131,072-token configuration. Tested 2026-10-12/13 on a Jetson Orin Nano 8 GB (JetPack R36.4.7, aarch64) with the GUI stopped, using the standard 34-prompt A-D suite (cap profile v3, temp 0.3 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 40, exec_check code executed not inspected).

Model: MiniCPM5-2B (OpenBMB, Apache 2.0) - 2.52B dense, LlamaForCausalLM, 42 layers, 2 KV heads (8:1 GQA), native context 131,072. Target quant Q4_K_M (1.56 GB). DSpark draft: 323.8M params, 5 layers, dflash arch, Q4_K_M (186 MB).
1. Executive Summary

rows: 84.3 tok/s - fastest measured on this box

elements.text: Verdict in one line: MiniCPM5-2B is not a Qwen3.5-2B replacement for the resident agent slot on raw quality, but with DSpark it is the fastest 2B-class generation engine tested on this hardware, and its 2-KV-head architecture makes it the only model that can run a full 128K window on an 8 GB Jetson.
2. Test Configurations
2.1 Baseline run (64K)

rows: 6.0 s to healthy; 3.41 GB RSS steady

elements.text: 2.2 Maxed run (131K + DSpark)

rows: -b 256 -ub 256 (reduced from 512 to fit draft compute buffers)
8.0 s to healthy; 5.74 GB RSS; 8.0 GB total DRAM, GUI off

elements.text: Note: the first maxed launch OOM-killed the draft's compute buffer at -ub 512 (272 MiB cudaMalloc failure). Dropping to -ub 256 and the Q4_K_M draft resolved it.
3. Speed Results
3.1 Baseline, no drafter (64K, 34 prompts)
Prompt processing averaged 431 tok/s; TTFT averaged 0.14 s. Tool-call bursts (17-46 tokens) dipped to 18-19 tok/s. Zero truncations across all 34 prompts.
3.2 DSpark speculative decoding (suite A, apples-to-apples)

Acceptance behavior (from server logs): 16.4% acceptance cold on the first generation, warming to 39-43% with mean accepted draft length 3.99 of the 7-token block. Content matters: code (repetitive syntax) reached 84.3 tok/s (3.2x) while freeform prose reached 31-40 tok/s (1.2-1.6x). Quick probes: essay 31.0, code 57.4, short reasoning 53.8 tok/s.

Draft overhead is negligible in memory (186 MB weights + 167 MB KV). DSpark is distributionally lossless: the target model still decides every accepted token. Temp-0.3 outputs differ between runs (sampling noise, not draft artifacts).
4. Quality (64K suite, graded 1-10 vs grade_key)

rows: sqrt(2) proof 10/10, clinical prose 8/10, iambic pentameter 2/10
induction proof 9/10, c_python exec pass 9/10; sqlite refusal 0/10
batball 10, sum100 10, sqrt2 9, fib 10; strawberry 2, elephant 1

elements.text: 4.1 Objective verification (exec_check: executed, not inspected)

rows: PASS - runs clean; correct dept averages (HR 75k / Eng 90k), top-3 output
PASS - runs clean; avg 86.25, top Diana, bottom Charlie
PASS - verified programmatically: fib(10)=55, fib(30)=832040 in <0.1 s

elements.text: 4.2 Function calling (C-suite)

Tool names and arguments were correct on every call attempted. The single failure is a guardrail-style refusal ('...or access patient information') on a benign agentic task - a training artifact, not a capability gap.
5. Deep Needle at Full Window (121K)

Needle construction identical to the LFM2.5 runbook: needle sentence at position ~0, 7,140 repetitions of the logistics filler, question last. Filler packing measured on MiniCPM's own tokenizer: 17.01 tokens/line (matching LFM's 17.0, versus ~26 on Qwen-class tokenizers). Greedy decoding (temp 0).

Interpretation: exact-token recall across a 121K window, inside the model's 131K native training boundary. This mirrors LFM2.5's pattern - exact recall within native context, degradation beyond it (LFM dropped to 'PINECONE' at 49.3K vs its 32K native). MiniCPM5-2B is the first model tested on this box whose native window makes a 128K deployment meaningful, and the first to pass a needle at >120K depth on 8 GB.
6. Findings
F1 - Letter-counting blind spot

Both counting traps failed with confident, wrong enumeration: '4 r's' in strawberry (a phantom 4th r) and '3 e's' in elephant (a hallucinated third e). Qwen3.5-2B passes both. Treat letter/character-counting tasks as out-of-scope for this model.
F2 - Refusals on benign tasks

2 of 34 prompts refused benign requests: the sqlite function call and 'why does ice float' ('cannot answer without context'). Also failed the piano tuners Fermi estimate by treating it as a joke (answered zero). Over-tuned guardrails directly reduce agentic reliability.
F3 - Stochastic repetition pathology

One strawberry smoke run looped 'but wait...' re-verification to the 3072-token cap despite a correct early answer (9 'wait' markers); the recorded run miscounted instead of looping. Both iambic prompts degenerated into repeated phrases. Repeat_penalty 1.0 (standard) was used; watch long generations for loops.
F4 - Thinking is on by default

Out of the box the model streams reasoning (63 tokens on a trivial question; a full 3072-cap burn on one trap). The embedded switch enable_thinking:false works cleanly through llama.cpp chat_template_kwargs and matches the Qwen3.5-2B graded configuration.
F5 - Memory and cursor champion

2 KV heads give 43 KB/token KV cost: 1.41 GB at 64K, 2.82 GB at 131K (q8_0). The 3.41 GB RSS at 64K is the leanest ever measured here (LFM2.5: 4.84 GB), and the 131K full-window load fits 8 GB with the GUI off.
F6 - DSpark transforms speed

2.0x on suite A average (52.3 vs 25.95 tok/s), up to 3.2x on code (84.3 tok/s - the fastest generation ever measured on this Jetson, versus Qwen3.5-2B's MTP peak of 46.6). Draft costs only 353 MB total.
7. Model Comparison (same suite, caps, sampling)
8. Verdict and Recommendations

As the resident Hermes-agent model: NO. Qwen3.5-2B remains the right choice - higher quality (7.4 vs 6.5), faster with MTP at short agentic generations, and it passes the traps MiniCPM5 misses. MiniCPM5's two refusals on benign tasks are disqualifying for an unattended agent loop.

Where MiniCPM5-2B wins: (1) long-context workloads - it is the only model that holds a true 128K window on 8 GB, with verified exact recall at 121K; (2) bulk generation with DSpark - 2x on prose, 3.2x on code, at a trivial memory cost; (3) memory-constrained deployments needing headroom alongside other services.

Recommended follow-ups: (a) rerun the interrupted max-token probe (32K-token long-form generation) to characterize the repetition loop at length; (b) a greedy A/B with and without the draft to document strict losslessness; (c) try --spec-draft-n-max beyond 7 (the draft was trained with block 7, but the scheduler may accept longer chains on code).

Outstanding item from the maxed session: the 32,768-token max-output probe was interrupted by a gateway shutdown mid-generation (server-side connection drop, no results recorded). Everything else in this report is backed by saved raw data in the project directory.
Appendix A - Methodology

Suite: canonical 34-prompt A-D suite (prompts_abcd.json, verbatim across all models): A general x5, B one-shot coding x5 (HTML/Python/C/TRS-80 BASIC/Julia), C zoo/ornith x12 (incl. 6 function-call with tool schemas), D reasoning traps x12. Cap profile v3: A 6500, B 24000 (deep-budget probe), C 4096 with function-calls at 1024, D 3072. Sampling: temp 0.3, top_p 0.95, top_k 40, min_p 0.0, repeat_penalty 1.0, streaming. exec_check code was executed, never inspected. Needle tests greedy (temp 0). Hard traps graded >= 7/10.

Harnesses: bench.py (live-server streaming, resume-safe JSONL, per-prompt ttft/pp/gen tok/s) adapted from the qwen35-2b benchmark; needle_128k.py (filler sized via /tokenize on the model's own tokenizer). Launches detached via Popen(start_new_session=True) per the long-batch runbook; the GUI (gdm3) was stopped for all runs. Raw data: results/bench_minicpm5_20261012.jsonl (34 rows), results/bench_minicpm5_131k_dspark_A.jsonl (5 rows), results/needle_121k.json, results/grades_minicpm5_20261012.json, results/responses/ (34 transcripts), results/exec/ (executed code + outputs).
